deferred.title: Exponential growth, doubling time, life-table and projection models
deferred.reason: Out of scope for this batch: exponential growth and doubling-time forms need log/exp support and a separate growth-rate record; age-specific fertility/mortality schedules need family (array) quantities; cohort-component projections need multi-model composition. Priority continuation after b03: crude birth/death subdivisions by sex if sourced.

gaps: New quantity meanings needed: demography:sex_ratio (males per 100 females, unit 1), demography:crude_net_migration_rate (per 1000, unit 1), demography:child_woman_ratio (children 0-4 per 1000 women 15-49, unit 1), demography:natural_increase_count (persons, unit 1). Per-100 and per-1000 presentation multipliers are explicit numeric literals with output unit 1, matching b01/b02 convention. Decimal-ratio presentations (e.g., SRB 1.05) are unit-convention variants, not separate models.
handoff.review_notes: b03 complements b01 (CBR, CDR, TDR, balance) and b02 (RNI, YDR, ODR, net migration count). Sex ratio uses PRB per-100 definition; SRB 105 figure is the same relationship applied to a birth cohort, documented in inverse_notes/summary, not a separate model. CNMR Germany-2023 oracle combines Destatis flow table (I, E) with Destatis year-end stocks for the average-population denominator; UN WPP 2024 Germany-2023 estimate may differ slightly in level. CWR Burkina Faso 1996 oracle is from the IUSSP teaching exercise (US Census Bureau International Database inputs), result 876 stated on site. Eurostat net-migration residual/measurement caveat recorded in limitations.
handoff.summary: Batch b03 adds four demography models: population sex ratio (per 100), crude net-migration rate (per 1000), child-woman ratio (per 1000 women 15-49), and natural-increase count (births minus deaths). All four validate as requires-extension (new demography meanings).

assumptions: source assumption: sex ratio is a stock measure of the living population at a reference date (PRB wording: 'in a population', no reference period).
source assumption: the per-100 multiplier is a presentation convention; the underlying index is the male/female ratio.

gaps: Meaning demography:sex_ratio and per-100 presentation convention need runtime extension; runtime_model null.

models.inverse_notes: Solve F = 100*M/SR requires SR != 0 (a zero sex ratio would mean no males; guard M >= 0 admits M = 0 with SR = 0, in which case F is unidentified). Solve M = SR*F/100 is linear, no singularity. Substitution check: SR = 103.2, F = 4700000 gives M = 103.2*4700000/100 = 4850400, within rounding of 4850000. Same relationship applied to a birth cohort gives the sex ratio at birth (benchmark ~105 males per 100 females); the decimal presentation (1.05) is a unit-convention variant, not a separate model. No causal invertibility: the ratio does not identify cohort histories.
limitations: Some agencies publish the inverse (females per 100 males); such figures must be inverted before comparison.
The ratio alone does not distinguish a high-SRB cohort effect from differential mortality or migration by sex.

references.method: Independent arithmetic illustration of the per-100 formula built from the research (same 103.2 structure as the worked example); checks the expression, not a published aggregate.

Benchmark case from the sources: OWID/UN WPP states about 105 boys are born for every 100 girls, inside the World Bank 1.03-1.07 normal band; inputs are the canonical per-100 illustration of that benchmark.
Limiting identity: equal numbers of males and females give exactly 100 by construction of the per-100 convention.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero female population violates F > 0; the ratio is undefined.
Female count missing; the ratio cannot be computed from males alone.

assumptions: source assumption: net migration is immigrants minus emigrants during the year (UN WPP wording).
source assumption: denominator is the average (midyear) population of that year, e.g. (P_Jan1_t + P_Jan1_t+1)/2.
application profile: the Germany-2023 oracle uses Destatis flow counts with a stock-averaged denominator; UN WPP estimates for the same year may differ slightly in level.

constants.locator: UN WPP dataportal indicator metadata: 'The value is expressed per 1000 persons'
constants.meaning: per-1000 presentation multiplier for the crude rate

gaps: Meaning demography:crude_net_migration_rate and per-1000 presentation convention need runtime extension; runtime_model null. Complements (not duplicates) demography--net-migration-count (b02 level) and demography--population-balance (b01).

models.inverse_notes: Given CNMR and P, net migration count N = CNMR*P/1000 (linear, exact up to rounding); substitution check: 7.84*84514086/1000 = 662590, within 0.1% of published 662964. I and E individually are NOT identified from the rate alone (one equation, two unknowns) -- a common misinversion. Zero/ambiguous case: CNMR = 0 with P finite admits any I = E, including zero gross flows.
limitations: Crude means denominated by total population with no age-sex standardisation; weakly comparable across different age structures.

Eurostat practice derives net migration residually (population change minus natural change), so the published 'net migration plus statistical adjustment' absorbs count errors and may include non-migration residuals.
Where flow data are insufficient, net migration may be estimated from stock differences (foreign-born/foreign-population) or as growth minus natural increase; inputs then carry that method's error.

references.method: Published inputs: Destatis migration flow table 2023 (arrivals 1932509, departures 1269545, net 662964) with average population from Destatis year-end stocks 2022/2023 (84358845, 84669326). 662964/84514086*1000 = 7.844; tolerance covers rounding of the averaged denominator.
Independent worked case in the standard textbook form (midyear population with flows): (200000-100000)/1050000*1000 = 95.238; checks the expression on materially different values.
Limiting identity: equal immigration and emigration give exactly zero net migration and hence a zero rate.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero average population violates P > 0; a rate over no population is undefined.
Immigration count missing; net migration cannot be formed from emigration and population alone.

assumptions: source assumption: numerator is surviving children aged 0-4 of both sexes as enumerated at the reference date (a stock, not a flow of births).
source assumption: denominator is women of reproductive age 15-49 (UNSD/IUSSP); PRB also admits 15-44, which is a different denominator and not interchangeable.
application profile: the Burkina Faso oracle uses 1996 census stocks; the ratio reflects recent fertility net of child mortality plus census coverage effects.

models.inverse_notes: Given CWR and C04, W = C04*1000/CWR requires CWR != 0. Given CWR and W, C04 = CWR*W/1000. Substitution check: 876*2303180/1000 = 2017585.7, within 0.05% of published 2016960 (rounding of the published ratio). No causal invertibility: the ratio understates true fertility (counts survivors only) and is depressed by young-child under-enumeration, so it cannot be inverted into a total fertility rate without a mortality/coverage model.
limitations: Invariably understates true fertility: counts surviving children only, so high-mortality settings read lower than their birth flow (UNSD).
Depressed by young-child census under-enumeration and age misreporting; narrowed across countries because high-fertility places also have high child mortality (UNSD).
Partly (not fully) standardised for age-sex composition; unlike CBR it still embeds population-structure effects (IUSSP: more a measure of 'youngness'/child-support burden).

references.method: Published teaching-oracle inputs: IUSSP PAPP101 Session 2 Exercise 2 (US Census Bureau International Database), children 0-4 = 2016960, women 15-49 = 2303180; stated correct answer 876. 2016960/2303180*1000 = 875.8; tolerance covers the unit rounding of the published ratio.
Independent ordinary case: 500/2000*1000 = 250 exactly; checks the expression on materially different values.
Limiting identity: zero surviving young children give exactly zero regardless of denominator.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero women of reproductive age violates W > 0; the ratio is undefined.
Denominator (women 15-49) missing; the ratio cannot be formed from the child count alone.

assumptions: source assumption: natural increase is the surplus (or deficit) of live births over deaths in the same period and territory (Eurostat wording).
application profile: inputs are period flow counts; the same identity holds for annual estimates, intercensal intervals, or projections provided B and D share period and territory.

gaps: Meaning demography:natural_increase_count needs runtime extension; runtime_model null. Complements (not duplicates) demography--natural-increase-rate (b02 per-1000 rate) and demography--population-balance (b01, which adds this difference to migration).

models.inverse_notes: Solve B = NI + D given deaths; solve D = B - NI given births. Both linear, no singularities. Substitution check: NI = 150000 with D = 750000 gives B = 900000. Zero case B = D gives NI = 0 regardless of level (a large balanced population still has zero natural increase). No causal invertibility: the count does not identify age-specific fertility or mortality schedules.
limitations: Counts alone do not standardise for population size or age structure; for comparison use the crude natural-increase rate (b02).
Does not separate the fertility and mortality contributions; equal and opposite changes in B and D leave NI unchanged.

references.method: Independent ordinary case: 900000 - 750000 = 150000 exactly; checks the expression on a plain surplus.
Independent materially different case: deaths exceed births, 500000 - 700000 = -200000; checks signed output (natural decrease).
Limiting identity: equal births and deaths give exactly zero natural increase.

rejection_cases.reason: Negative birth count violates B >= 0; counts of vital events cannot be negative.
Death count missing; natural increase cannot be formed from births alone.

relationship.locator: Eurostat demo_gind metadata: natural change = live births minus deaths; corroborated by the balancing equation (b01 sources: PRB glossary, World Bank WDI methodology)
relationship.original_equation: Natural change / natural increase: the difference between the number of live births and the number of deaths during the period (Eurostat).
relationship.translation_notes: Dimensional check: persons minus persons = persons (unit 1). This is the level form; the b02 rate form divides by midyear population and scales per 1000, and the b01 balance adds net migration to this difference.

sources.evidence: Reference metadata define natural change as live births minus deaths during the year, and the crude rate of natural change as that difference over average population per 1000; births and deaths follow the usual-residence and vital-events definitions.
